A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Value-Spectrum and retain matching datasets, methods, and main experiments. All supplied pages are readable. v1 ends after the references despite mentioning an appendix; v2 includes Appendices A-G, whose contents can be assessed as newly documented material.

before.justification: v1 reports original VLM preference scores, persona-induction experiments, visual-versus-text comparisons, and human screenshot validation in Table 1, Figures 8-9, and Section 6.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds keyword-level scores, detailed persona-induction results, and caption-source comparisons in its appendices.

M1.justification: Screenshot retrieval, binary preference scoring, and the Simple and ISQ persona-induction strategies remain substantively unchanged, including the ISQ score and threshold. The fuller prompts and timing specifications document the existing procedure rather than establish a new method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 50,191 social-media records from TikTok, YouTube, and Instagram, the ten Schwartz values, and Persona-Chat personas. The appendices retain these tasks and domains; additional caption configurations and revised sample counts do not expand dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: The six evaluated VLMs, Simple/ISQ strategies, and three text-model counterparts in the modality comparison remain the same. Table 18 varies caption-source inputs for retained models rather than adding a new model baseline. InCharacter is newly cited but not evaluated.

E3.justification: Section 6 changes human validation from 500 images total and 1,500 ratings to 500 images per platform and 4,500 ratings. This is a substantive reported sample-size revision, without establishing that additional annotation occurred. Table 18 also adds caption-source/model combinations to the modality evaluation.

E4.justification: Appendix E and Table 18 extend the existing visual-versus-text sensitivity analysis with comparisons across caption generators and answering models. Appendix C explains the single-frame choice but reports no actual single-versus-multiple-frame ablation.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same means and standard deviations in Table 1, retain the dispersion plot in Figure 7, and specify ten persona-induction trials. No new seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedure are reported.

E6.justification: Tables 2-11 add keyword-level preferences, Tables 12-17 add first/last-window rates, and Table 18 adds a detailed caption-source/model result matrix. Table 1 and the 90.4% representative/8.8% non-representative findings remain unchanged. Some added entries conflict with retained plots: Table 15 reports +1.9% for Qwen-VL-Plus under YouTube ISQ, while Figure 8 remains negative.

T1.justification: The preference average, persona-alignment metric, and ISQ composite-score formula remain mathematically unchanged. The explicit decision display is removed, but its threshold remains stated. Neither version supplies additional theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a social-media benchmark for Schwartz-value preferences, distinct model preference patterns, and persona induction through Simple and ISQ prompting. The condensed conclusion and clearer screenshot terminology do not materially change these contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix C adds substantive reasons for single-frame processing, particularly that multi-frame latency could lengthen viewing and confound recommendation feedback. Section 9 also acknowledges potentially biased outputs. Existing limitations concerning Schwartz-value coverage and complex videos remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a dataset-download reference, identifies CLIP for retrieval, and supplies complete formatted prompts, two-second screenshot timing, and 45-second viewing actions. It also documents balanced modality sampling, MTurk piloting, annotator instructions, and compensation. These substantially fill implementation and reproducibility gaps in v1.

R1.justification: v2 adds InCharacter to the introductory role-playing context and supplies industry references about recommendation signals in Appendix A. The broader research positioning remains stable. The two Chen et al. entries refer to the same survey already cited in v1.

P1.justification: The abstract and introductory framing are extensively rewritten, the conclusion is condensed, and terminology is standardized throughout the main text. v2 also changes the title and author line and introduces an organized A-G appendix, while retaining the main section order.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 2-18 and Figures 10-15, including detailed results, response examples, and annotation instructions. Figure 2 gains example screenshots, and Figure 8 is redrawn with revised model labels but loses its Simple/ISQ panel labels. Several other core figures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added access information, complete prompts, timing details, annotation instructions, and granular results make v2 easier to inspect and reproduce than v1. However, the new tables are not consistently reconciled with retained plots, notably Table 15 versus Figure 8, and the human-study sample-count revision is unexplained. These shortcomings limit the overall gain despite substantial improvements in documentation.
